source_review.notes: Checked current AWS API Gateway token-bucket/throttling guidance, Envoy local/global limiter semantics, NGINX rate-limiting guidance, current IETF HTTPAPI RateLimit Internet-Draft status, RFC 6585 status 429, RFC 9110 Retry-After and the cited traffic-regulation, reliability, queueing and performance sources. Managed limits and the draft header fields are explicitly qualified.

evidence: Checked key, token, capacity, refill, cost, timestamps, interval admission, replica count, hierarchy and distributed-error notation.
Checked lazy-refill/spend, ideal interval bound, Little's-Law counterexample and local-replica multiplication equations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Rate, burst, concurrency and long-period quota remain distinct dimensions.

evidence: Reproduced the executable trace: five initial admits then reject; one token refills by 500 ms and admits; at 1,000 ms one token cannot pay cost two; by 3,000 ms capacity refills to five and cost five admits; 7 allowed, 2 rejected, 0 remaining.
Recomputed ideal three-second bound B+rΔ = 5+2(3)=11 cost units.
Recomputed Exercise 2: floor(30/4)=7 immediate complete requests, 2 tokens remain, and 30+6(10)=90 cost upper bound.
Recomputed Exercise 3: five local buckets provide about 200/s and aggregate initial burst 400, not global 40/s and 80.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Interval cost bounds do not promise a number of complete requests or production capacity.

evidence: Verified ideal token conservation from capacity-clamped refill and atomic cost spend yields B+rΔ bound.
Verified rate alone cannot bound residents when residence is unbounded and verified n independent buckets sum to n(B+rΔ).
Verified atomic all-or-nothing hierarchical spend conditionally preserves each bucket constraint and bounded key admission is required to bound state cardinality.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Proofs assume one monotonic atomic state, correct costs and declared distributed error; they do not calibrate capacity.

evidence: Reviewed empty/full/partial, exact equality, cost above capacity, discrete/continuous refill, fixed/sliding boundary, zero/backward/large elapsed, precision and overflow.
Reviewed concurrent overspend, hierarchy partial spend/rollback, weighted/unknown streaming cost, token refund, finite wait/defer, deadlines and retries.

Reviewed untrusted identity, NAT/botnet/key spray, eviction/cold start, per-replica scale, shard remap, central-store partition, lease expiry, fail-open/closed, protocol metadata/privacy and safety-critical priority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real clocks, atomic stores, proxies, workloads, distribution, security and safety require integration/fault evidence and named review.

evidence: Traced declared policy/key/unit/algorithm, authenticated bounded identity, atomic spend, monotonic refill, atomic hierarchy and pre-work rejection through exposition/examples/answers.
Traced finite wait/defer, cost/capacity calibration, distributed overshoot, cold-state lifecycle and advisory privacy-safe feedback.
invariant_checking.notes: The limiter is never presented as concurrency isolation or a service-capacity proof.

evidence: Reviewed token-conservation, concurrency counterexample, local multiplication, hierarchical safety and cardinality-bound arguments against explicit premises.
Reviewed why fixed-window and distributed/local enforcement claims require trace/error semantics.
Confirmed no-capacity-proof limitation follows because configuration is external to algorithm correctness.
proof_review.notes: No formal proof of concrete distributed storage, fairness, downstream safety, security or high-stakes operation is claimed.

evidence: Audited exact, global, bounded, atomic, fair, authoritative, standard, safe, guarantee and proof language.
Confirmed the RateLimit document is labeled active Internet-Draft/work in progress and managed-platform best-effort semantics are not elevated into hard ceilings.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Advisory response metadata is not represented as a promise of future admission.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/SEPAT-085/report.json
Reproduced nine sequential milli-token decisions, allowed/rejected counts, terminal balance and ideal interval arithmetic using Python 3.
Confirmed the block performs no concurrency, authentication, state eviction, networking, distributed coordination, queueing or protected work.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes one fixed integer trace only.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter treats Rate Limiter as an authenticated temporal cost-admission contract with explicit burst, hierarchy and distributed error, not a requests-per-second slogan.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers token/fixed/sliding/GCRA algorithms, rate-versus-concurrency/quota, keys/cardinality, weighted cost, hierarchy, distributed architectures, protocol/client behavior, telemetry, security and fault testing.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with conditional proofs, exact milli-token trace, ten distinct cases and five exercises progressing from policy design through arithmetic, distributed tradeoffs, diagnosis and safety-critical judgment.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
